title: Acts Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 12.

questions.question: In Acts 12, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Herod stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church
James was killed with the sword
The angel of the Lord came upon Peter
questions.correctAnswer: Herod stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church
questions.explanation: This event is mentioned first in the chapter, specifically in Acts 12:1.

questions.question: Who did Herod kill with the sword?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:2 states that Herod killed James the brother of John with the sword.

questions.question: Why did Herod proceed to take Peter also?
options: It was the days of unleavened bread
He saw it pleased the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: He saw it pleased the Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 12:3 states that Herod proceeded to take Peter because he saw it pleased the Jews.

questions.question: How many soldiers did Herod deliver Peter to in prison?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:4 mentions that Herod delivered Peter to four quaternions of soldiers.

questions.question: What was made without ceasing for Peter?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:5 indicates that prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for Peter.

questions.question: Where was Peter sleeping when he was apprehended?
questions.explanation: According to Acts 12:6, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers.

questions.question: What happened to Peter's chains when the angel of the Lord came?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:7 states that Peter's chains fell off from his hands.

questions.question: What did the angel instruct Peter to do first?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:8 mentions that the angel said unto Peter, 'Gird thyself.'

questions.question: What did Peter think when he followed the angel?
options: He thought it was a vision
questions.correctAnswer: He thought it was a vision
questions.explanation: Acts 12:9 states that Peter followed the angel but thought he saw a vision.

questions.question: Was Peter kept in prison?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:5 clearly states that Peter was kept in prison.

questions.question: Did Herod intend to bring Peter forth after Easter?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:4 indicates that Herod intended to bring Peter forth after Easter.

questions.question: Is it true that Herod killed James?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:2 confirms that Herod killed James the brother of John.

questions.question: Is it true that Peter was sleeping between two soldiers?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:6 states that Peter was sleeping between two soldiers.

questions.question: Is it false that prayer was made for Peter by the church?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:5 shows that prayer was indeed made without ceasing of the church for Peter.

questions.question: Is it false that the angel of the Lord left Peter in prison?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:7 reveals that the angel of the Lord came upon Peter and helped him escape from prison.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the iron gate do when Peter approached it?
options: It opened to them of its own accord
questions.correctAnswer: It opened to them of its own accord
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in Acts 12:10, which says, 'which opened to them of his own accord.'

questions.question: What does Acts 12:12 promise will happen if someone prays without ceasing?
options: They will be delivered from prison
questions.explanation: Acts 12:5 indicates that prayer was made without ceasing, which implies that God hears and responds to such prayer.

questions.question: What was Peter's reaction when he realized he had been delivered from prison?
options: He said he knew the Lord sent his angel
questions.correctAnswer: He said he knew the Lord sent his angel
questions.explanation: Peter acknowledges in Acts 12:11 that he knows for sure that the Lord has sent his angel to deliver him.

questions.question: What does Acts 12:17 indicate Peter instructed the people to do?
options: Go show these things unto James and the brethren
questions.correctAnswer: Go show these things unto James and the brethren
questions.explanation: In Acts 12:17, Peter specifically tells them to inform James and the brethren about his escape.

questions.question: How did the soldiers react when they found Peter missing?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:18 explains that there was no small stir among the soldiers regarding what had become of Peter, indicating their confusion.

questions.question: What did Rhoda do when she recognized Peter's voice?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:14 shows that instead of opening the gate, Rhoda ran in to tell others about Peter standing at the gate.

questions.question: What was the initial reaction of those praying when Rhoda told them about Peter?
options: They told her to be quiet
questions.explanation: Acts 12:15 indicates that the people thought Rhoda was mad when she claimed Peter was at the gate.

questions.question: What did Peter do while the others were initially doubting Rhoda's claim?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:16 states that Peter continued knocking at the door while they were debating Rhoda's claim.

questions.question: What did Peter tell the believers to do after he was let in?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:17 shows that Peter instructed them to let others know what had happened, particularly James and the brethren.

questions.question: What does Peter's escape demonstrate about the power of prayer?
options: It can lead to miraculous events
It is always answered the way we expect
It is ineffective in dire situations
It should be done in secret
questions.correctAnswer: It can lead to miraculous events
questions.explanation: Peter's escape from prison, following the church's prayers, exemplifies the power of prayer to bring about miraculous outcomes.

questions.question: What was Peter's state of mind while imprisoned, according to Acts 12:6?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:6 describes Peter as sleeping between two soldiers while bound with chains, indicating his peace despite the circumstances.

questions.question: What does Peter's story teach about God's deliverance?
options: It can come in unexpected ways
It is dependent on our actions
It is rare in difficult situations
questions.correctAnswer: It can come in unexpected ways
questions.explanation: Peter's unexpected and miraculous deliverance from prison illustrates that God's ways of delivering us can be surprising and beyond our understanding.

questions.question: Is it true that the church was praying continuously for Peter's release?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:5 confirms that prayer was made without ceasing by the church unto God for Peter.

questions.question: Is it true that Peter initially believed he was dreaming during his escape?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:9 states that Peter did not realize it was true, indicating he was confused, not necessarily believing he was dreaming.

questions.question: Is it true that the angel told Peter to follow him after his chains fell off?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:8 records that the angel instructed Peter to gird himself and bind on his sandals, which indicates preparation, but does not explicitly say 'follow me' until later.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 12.

questions.question: What did Herod command to be done to the keepers of the prison after he could not find Peter?
options: They should be put to death
They should be punished with lashes
questions.correctAnswer: They should be put to death
questions.explanation: Herod commanded that they should be put to death because he could not find Peter after seeking for him. (Acts 12:19)

questions.question: Why were the people of Tyre and Sidon seeking peace with Herod?
options: Because they wanted to praise him
Because their country was nourished by the king's country
questions.correctAnswer: Because their country was nourished by the king's country
questions.explanation: The people of Tyre and Sidon desired peace with Herod because their country was nourished by the king's country. (Acts 12:20)

questions.question: What did Herod do on the set day while arrayed in royal apparel?
options: He made an oration unto them
questions.correctAnswer: He made an oration unto them
questions.explanation: Herod sat upon his throne and made an oration unto the people while arrayed in royal apparel. (Acts 12:21)

questions.question: What did the people proclaim about Herod after he spoke?
options: It is the voice of a god, and not of a man
questions.correctAnswer: It is the voice of a god, and not of a man
questions.explanation: The people shouted that Herod's voice was that of a god, not a man. (Acts 12:22)

questions.question: What happened to Herod immediately after he did not give God the glory?
options: He was smote by an angel of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: He was smote by an angel of the Lord
questions.explanation: The angel of the Lord smote Herod because he did not give God the glory, resulting in him being eaten of worms. (Acts 12:23)

questions.question: What was the outcome of the word of God after these events?
questions.explanation: Despite the persecution and events surrounding Herod, the word of God grew and multiplied. (Acts 12:24)

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'oratio' in Acts 12:21 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'oratio' refers to 'speech', as Herod made an oration to the people. (Acts 12:21)

questions.question: Which literary device is used when the people shout Herod's glory?
questions.explanation: The people's proclamation that Herod's voice is that of a god is an example of exaggeration, emphasizing their reverence. (Acts 12:22)

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of divine judgment as seen with Herod's fate?
questions.explanation: Daniel 4:30 recounts a similar theme of divine judgment when King Nebuchadnezzar was judged for his pride, paralleling Herod's fate. (Acts 12:23)

questions.question: Which other passage discusses the growth of the word of God, echoing Acts 12:24?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:2 encourages believers to desire the pure milk of the word, echoing the growth of the word of God mentioned in Acts 12:24. (Acts 12:24)

questions.question: What comes immediately before the statement about Herod's displeasure in Acts 12:20?
options: The angel of the Lord smote him
questions.explanation: Before Herod's displeasure, he examined the keepers regarding Peter's escape. (Acts 12:19-20)

questions.question: What event is described immediately after Peter's escape in Acts 12:11?
options: He went to the house of Mary
questions.correctAnswer: He went to the house of Mary
questions.explanation: After realizing he was freed, Peter went to the house of Mary, where many were gathered in prayer. (Acts 12:12)

questions.question: The people of Tyre and Sidon sought peace with Herod; this reflects what broader biblical theme?
questions.explanation: Their desire for peace with Herod illustrates the theme of submission to authority, recognizing his power. (Acts 12:20)

questions.question: The assertion that Herod was eaten of worms is a metaphorical expression. True or False?
questions.explanation: This is true; it serves as a metaphor for divine judgment and Herod's fate due to pride. (Acts 12:23)

questions.question: The word of God shrinking in power is a theme in Acts 12. True or False?
questions.explanation: This is false; the word of God grew and multiplied, indicating its increasing power. (Acts 12:24)

theological.title: Acts Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 12:5 teach about the role of prayer in the life of the church?
options: Prayer is a continual intercession for believers under persecution
Prayer is only necessary before major events
Prayer replaces all other forms of action
Prayer is ineffective without visible results
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer is a continual intercession for believers under persecution
questions.explanation: Acts 12:5 states that 'prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him,' showing the doctrine that the church perseveres in continual intercessory prayer especially in times of trial.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine deliverance does Acts 12:7 teach?
options: God sovereignly intervenes to deliver His people miraculously
Deliverance is always through human means
God never intervenes in earthly affairs
Deliverance depends on human strength alone
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly intervenes to deliver His people miraculously
questions.explanation: Acts 12:7 describes an angel of the Lord coming to free Peter from prison, illustrating that God's deliverance can be immediate and supernatural according to His sovereign will.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sin and divine judgment is taught in Acts 12:23?
options: God judges those who do not give Him glory
Human sin is overlooked by God
Divine judgment is arbitrary and random
questions.correctAnswer: God judges those who do not give Him glory
questions.explanation: Acts 12:23 shows that Herod was struck down by an angel because 'he gave not God the glory,' teaching that divine judgment is a just response to human pride and refusal to honor God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 12:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:10 describes the iron gate opening of its own accord, demonstrating God's sovereignty over natural and human constraints.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Acts 12:7 by the angel's intervention?
questions.explanation: The angel’s ability to break Peter’s chains and lead him out of prison in Acts 12:7 reflects God’s omnipotence, His unlimited power to act.

questions.question: How does the deliverance of Peter in Acts 12:6-11 connect to the broader biblical theme of God rescuing His people?
options: It prefigures Israel’s exodus from Egypt as a divine act of salvation
It contradicts the Old Testament idea of God’s rescue
It emphasizes human effort over divine action
It shows that deliverance is only symbolic
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Israel’s exodus from Egypt as a divine act of salvation
questions.explanation: The miraculous rescue of Peter echoes the theme of God rescuing His people seen in the Exodus narrative, highlighting God’s ongoing salvation history.

questions.question: In what way does Herod’s death in Acts 12:23 fulfill Old Testament warnings about pride and blasphemy?
options: It fulfills the warning that God resists the proud and punishes blasphemy
It contradicts Old Testament teachings on kingship
It shows that God ignores human pride
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the warning that God resists the proud and punishes blasphemy
questions.explanation: Herod’s demise for accepting divine honors in place of God demonstrates the Old Testament principle that God opposes the proud (cf. Proverbs 3:34), as shown in Acts 12:23.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 12:5 and Acts 12:7 teach about the relationship between prayer and divine intervention?
options: Persistent prayer is linked to God’s sovereign intervention
Prayer is unrelated to God’s actions
Divine intervention happens only without prayer
Prayer is a human attempt that God ignores
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent prayer is linked to God’s sovereign intervention
questions.explanation: Acts 12:5 shows the church praying without ceasing, and Acts 12:7 shows God responding by sending an angel, indicating that persistent prayer is connected to God's sovereign acts.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human unbelief and spiritual perception is taught by comparing Acts 12:9 and Acts 12:11?
options: Believers may initially not recognize God’s work but come to assured faith
Belief is automatic and requires no reflection
Spiritual experiences are always clear at first
Faith is unnecessary to recognize God’s intervention
questions.correctAnswer: Believers may initially not recognize God’s work but come to assured faith
questions.explanation: Acts 12:9 shows Peter thinking it was a vision, but Acts 12:11 shows his firm conviction that God sent the angel, teaching that faith often follows initial spiritual confusion.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about the growth of the gospel can be drawn from Acts 12:24 and Acts 12:25?
options: Despite persecution, the gospel advances through faithful ministry
The gospel declines when leaders leave
Growth depends only on political favor
The gospel spreads regardless of God's blessing
questions.correctAnswer: Despite persecution, the gospel advances through faithful ministry
questions.explanation: Acts 12:24 states the word of God grew and multiplied, and 12:25 shows Barnabas and Saul completing their ministry, illustrating gospel growth amid opposition.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Acts 12:6-11 is a mythical story with no historical or theological value. What does Acts 12:6-11 actually teach?
options: It teaches the reality of divine intervention and the power of God to deliver His servants
It shows that all miraculous events are fabricated
It suggests that God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the reality of divine intervention and the power of God to deliver His servants
questions.explanation: Acts 12:6-11 narrates a miraculous angelic rescue, affirming God's active involvement in the lives of believers rather than myth or indifference.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 12:19 teach about human justice and divine sovereignty?
options: Human attempts at justice are limited and subject to God’s sovereign will
Human justice always reflects God’s perfect will
Human justice is ineffective and meaningless
questions.correctAnswer: Human attempts at justice are limited and subject to God’s sovereign will
questions.explanation: Acts 12:19 shows Herod kills the guards but fails to find Peter, indicating human justice is fallible and ultimately under God’s control.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Acts 12:24 concerning the progression of the gospel despite opposition?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:24 states 'the word of God grew and multiplied,' showing God’s faithfulness in ensuring the gospel’s progress despite challenges.

questions.question: What theological doctrine about God's providence is taught in Acts 12:20-21 regarding political and social events?
options: God’s providence extends over political alliances and human affairs
God is uninvolved in political matters
Political events are random and chaotic
Human politics operate independently of divine will
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence extends over political alliances and human affairs
questions.explanation: Acts 12:20-21 describes political maneuvers and Herod’s public address, implying that God’s providence governs even secular events.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about human unbelief and divine revelation is found in Acts 12:13-16?
options: Human disbelief can persist even amid direct evidence of God’s work
Unbelief is immediately overcome by miracles
Divine revelation always convinces everyone instantly
Faith is irrelevant to recognizing God’s interventions
questions.correctAnswer: Human disbelief can persist even amid direct evidence of God’s work
questions.explanation: The disbelief of those hearing Rhoda in Acts 12:15 despite her testimony, contrasted with their astonishment in 12:16, shows that unbelief can persist even when God acts clearly.
